subject.title: feat: add relyable scanner adapter (functional re-derivation evidence)

question: Should functional re-derivation become a supported built-in ClawScan scanner and should Relyable ship in the default Docker runtime?
rationale: The implementation introduces a public scanner ID, broadens the product beyond its stated security-scanning purpose, and adds a third-party dependency that executes target skill code; code review cannot choose that permanent support boundary.

options.title: Benchmark externally first
options.body: Require a representative benchmark submission and keep Relyable operator-installed until its signal value and maintenance burden justify built-in adoption.

options.title: Sponsor built-in adoption
options.body: Approve the new evidence axis and runtime dependency, then require a rebase plus packaged environment-isolation proof before merge.

options.title: Decline the new axis
options.body: Close the proposal if functional re-derivation should remain a standalone tool rather than part of ClawScan's supported scanner catalog.

recommendation.title: Benchmark externally first
recommendation.body: Require a representative benchmark submission and keep Relyable operator-installed until its signal value and maintenance burden justify built-in adoption.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate connected to scanner evaluation and benchmark direction, although final repository authority is not established by the available history.
